title: The Bioreactor Bid
primary_metric: liters of viable product yielded per dollar of vessel cost

options.A: The Column Bid — a standard cylindrical stirred-tank bioreactor
options.B: The Wave Bid — a wave/rocking bioreactor whose curved bag profile requires a disk-method volume calculation

_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC §4

deliverables.text: A net-cumulative-yield calculation for the batch — the area between the feed-rate curve and the uptake-rate curve from Appendix A, in liters of viable product per liter of working volume, with your work shown.

A working-volume calculation for each vessel at the target fill level: for the Column Bid, the cylinder-volume formula applied to Appendix B's dimensions; for the Wave Bid, the disk-method integral of the bag's cross-sectional profile from Appendix C, including a labeled diagram of the solid of revolution you integrated.
A total-yield table showing liters of viable product for each vessel option (D1's per-liter net yield multiplied by each vessel's D2 working volume).
A yield-per-dollar comparison: liters of viable product yielded per dollar of total vessel cost (vessel plus validation, from Appendices B, C, and D), for both options.
An original visual display of the feed-rate and uptake-rate curves from Appendix A, with the area you used in D1 shaded and labeled.

balance.argument_a: The Column Bid's cylindrical working volume is exact and fully usable at any fill level, and it is typically the cheaper vessel to buy and validate; the Wave Bid's curved bag profile always yields less usable volume than its nominal capacity once the disk-method integral is applied, and if its mixing-driven per-liter yield gain doesn't outrun that volume penalty plus its higher cost, the Column Bid wins on yield per dollar despite its lower density ceiling.
balance.argument_b: The Wave Bid's superior mixing raises the net cumulative yield per liter of working volume (a larger area between the feed-rate and uptake-rate curves), and because the primary metric is yield per dollar rather than yield per liter, a vessel that converts fewer liters into more product per liter can still win the ratio even after its cost and its disk-method-integrated volume shortfall are accounted for.
balance.margin_basis: Compare total liters of viable product yielded per dollar of total vessel cost (net cumulative yield per liter, from the area between Appendix A's feed-rate and uptake-rate curves, times each vessel's working volume — cylinder formula for the Column Bid, disk-method integral of Appendix C's bag profile for the Wave Bid — divided by vessel-plus-validation cost from Appendices B, C, and D) once case-research fills the open placeholders.
